items.title: THE FPL SCOUTCAST GAMEWEEK 12 WITH FPL CHAI 🚨 | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Calvert-Lewin emerges as the Gameweek 12 captaincy punt as Haaland and Palmer doubts grow
items.summary:
Gameweek 11 produces widespread low scores and red arrows as the usual FPL template underwhelms, although Bournemouth assets such as Antoine Semenyo, Tavernier and Antonio Silva reward owners. Attention now turns to a favourable six-gameweek fixture swing for Manchester City, Liverpool, Arsenal, Brighton, Chelsea and Aston Villa, but there is growing reluctance to hold premium names purely on fixture projections. Erling Haaland has strong recent underlying numbers but blanks in three straight matches, while Cole Palmer's form and Chelsea's overall performance create a genuine case to sell despite his long-term upside.

Manchester United are a major watchpoint under new manager Pochettino. Bruno Fernandes is a possible replacement for Palmer, particularly ahead of Brentford, Newcastle, Coventry and Crystal Palace, but the recommendation is to give United another week or two before committing heavily after their poor display against Liverpool. Bryan Mbeumo remains worth holding because he is not playing as defensively as feared, while a Palmer-to-Bruno move becomes more attractive around Gameweek 14 if managers plan to use a Free Hit then. Free Hit timing is central to transfer planning: Gameweek 14 allows managers to attack United's Coventry fixture and remove awkward fixtures, while Gameweek 16 remains an alternative.

Defenders remain the best value area of the game because DefCon points repeatedly turn cheap starters into eight-point candidates when combined with clean sheets. Arsenal are still the elite defence, but owners of Jurrien Timber/Calafiori-type rotation risks are encouraged to consider moving to established DefCon options. Bournemouth's Antonio Silva and James Hill, Leeds' Muharevic, Liverpool's Jeremy Jacquet, Brighton's Van Hecke and Spurs' Van de Ven are all viable depending on fixture rotation. Muharevic stands out for secure minutes, elite DefCon potential and Leeds' lack of European football, while Jacquet is a credible differential given Liverpool's run of Everton, Sunderland, Leeds, Spurs and Hull after a potential Gameweek 14 Free Hit.

Up front, the mid-priced options offer enough value to pair Haaland with two cheaper forwards. Evanilson continues to post elite expected-goal numbers for Bournemouth and is no longer easily dismissed as a fortunate finisher, while Calvert-Lewin is especially appealing for Leeds' home match against Coventry in Gameweek 12. Calvert-Lewin is the preferred captaincy differential, ahead of Haaland away to Arsenal, with Nicolas Jackson also a viable alternative at Ipswich. Jackson is more attractive for managers not Free Hitting in Gameweek 14; those using that chip then can buy Calvert-Lewin for Coventry before removing Leeds' difficult Manchester City and Liverpool fixtures.

David Raya's injury forces a goalkeeper discussion. Managers should ideally have a playable reserve rather than a £4.0m non-playing deputy, and Raya owners are advised to assess a short-term replacement rather than risk a zero. Guglielmo Vicario/Kinsky-type Spurs coverage at around £4.4m-£4.5m is favoured for Sunderland, Fulham and Hull, while Trafford is another strong option, though spending over £5m on a backup goalkeeper is considered excessive. The overall approach is to preserve transfers where possible, but use accumulated free transfers to fix dead bench spots, move on Chelsea uncertainty and buy a credible Gameweek 12 captain.
key_points: Captain Calvert-Lewin against Coventry in Gameweek 12 as the leading differential captaincy call, with Jackson at Ipswich the main alternative.
Haaland is a legitimate sell discussion after three blanks, but his Chelsea and Hull fixtures in Gameweeks 15-16 make managers wary of moving too early.

Palmer is no longer considered essential because Chelsea are struggling and his output does not justify his premium price, although Bruno Fernandes is best approached cautiously after another look at Manchester United.
Hold Mbeumo through Manchester United's favourable run because fears that he will become a defensive wing-back have not materialised.
Prioritise DefCon defenders with secure minutes: Muharevic, Antonio Silva, Jacquet, Van Hecke and James Hill are the principal targets.
A Gameweek 14 Free Hit strengthens the case for short-term buys such as Calvert-Lewin and allows aggressive investment in Manchester United for Coventry.
Raya is unlikely to be rushed back immediately after missing European action; upgrade a non-playing backup to a £4.4m-£4.5m goalkeeper such as Kinsky rather than overspend on a replacement.
Avoid carrying expensive dead bench options such as Gonzalo or Sangare when cheap DefCon defenders provide stronger rotation value.

items.title: My transfer tips ahead of Gameweek 12 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Hold Mbeumo, sell Schade as Liverpool midfielders lead Gameweek 12 targets
items.summary:
Goalkeeper news centres on Raya, who is not thought to be as badly injured as first feared and could return soon. Managers without a reliable second goalkeeper can consider Kinsky as short-term cover for the next couple of gameweeks, but Raya owners should not make a rushed long-term move if they can absorb his absence.

Keep Mbeumo if you already own him, although buying him now carries some risk because his minutes may be less secure under Pochettino. Howe-Lewan is a strong Gameweek 12 option, but managers need to plan around difficult away fixtures against Manchester City in Gameweek 13 and Liverpool in Gameweek 15, when benching him may be preferable. In defence, Murmovich gets the nod over Bogle because of his defensive-contribution potential, though Bogle remains a viable cheaper alternative. Oafur is avoided because his minutes are not trusted after a Gameweek 8 benching.

Van Hecke has been highly consistent, but prospective buyers should account for a worsening schedule from Gameweek 14 to 19, including Arsenal, Liverpool, Brighton, Bournemouth and Manchester City. For Liverpool midfield cover, Vert is the standout choice. Sparkler is also an option, but his £8.1m price makes the premium difficult to justify, while Sosa offers value at £6.7m, takes set pieces and may also be on penalties.

Kevin Scharder is a sell candidate after being benched against Everton. He may start in Gameweek 12, but his role is no longer secure; Rodoni or Enzo Lefay are the preferred replacements for managers unable to spend more. Man Zambi remains a hold despite an early Gameweek 11 substitution because he continues to start, whereas McInn is more concerning after two benchings in five gameweeks. There is no need to panic-sell McInn before Gameweek 12, but he should be moved on when a spare transfer is available.
key_points: Raya could return soon, so Kinsky is mainly a short-term cover option for managers without a playing backup goalkeeper.
Keep Mbeumo if owned, but be cautious about buying because Pochettino may reduce his minute security.
Howe-Lewan is a strong Gameweek 12 pick, although Manchester City away in Gameweek 13 and Liverpool away in Gameweek 15 are likely benching fixtures.
Murmovich is preferred to the cheaper Bogle because of defensive contributions, while Oafur is avoided over unreliable minutes.
Van Hecke has been consistent, but his Gameweek 14-19 run includes Arsenal, Liverpool, Brighton, Bournemouth and Manchester City.
Vert is the preferred Liverpool midfielder; Sosa is a cheaper set-piece alternative, while Sparkler is hard to justify at £8.1m.
Sell Kevin Scharder if possible after his Everton benching, with Rodoni and Enzo Lefay preferred budget replacements.
Hold Man Zambi, but plan to sell McInn when convenient after two benchings in his last five gameweeks.

items.title: BEST FPL STRIKERS 🎯 |  FPL EXPERT GW12 TEAM REVEAL  ✅ | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Morgan Gibbs-White and Florian Wirtz lead Tom Freeman’s Gameweek 12 rebuild
items.summary:
Tom Freeman enters Gameweek 12 around 106k overall after a 27-point Gameweek 11, with four free transfers and £2.0m in the bank. His immediate concern is midfield, where Cole Palmer, Kevin Schade and Anton Stach are all causing problems: Palmer is expensive and badly out of form, while Schade and Stach carry minutes risk. Arsenal defensive cover is also becoming less appealing, with Riccardo Calafiori and Ezri Konsa facing uncertain starts around European fixtures.

The likely first moves are Schade and Stach out for Morgan Gibbs-White and a Liverpool midfielder, with Florian Wirtz preferred to Dominik Szoboszlai. Gibbs-White faces Chelsea in Gameweek 12 and offers security of starts, penalties and potential captaincy appeal, particularly if Moises Caicedo is absent. Wirtz is favoured for his open-play threat and multiple routes to returns, although Szoboszlai retains set-piece appeal. If funds are tight, Calafiori could be sold for Bournemouth’s Antonio Silva, leaving two free transfers for the midweek Gameweek 13 round.

Palmer is considered a clear eventual sell but not necessarily an urgent Gameweek 12 move. Chelsea face Crystal Palace before a much tougher run against Liverpool, Manchester City and Aston Villa, so Freeman’s likely plan is to retain Palmer briefly before using his funds to reshape the squad. Rodoni is identified as a possible Gameweek 13 replacement target ahead of Ipswich at home, due to his nailed minutes, penalties and all-round attacking involvement.

Nicolas Jackson currently has the captaincy against Ipswich, but Freeman sees Liverpool’s Alexander Isak as the stronger choice if owned, given Liverpool’s attack and Everton’s defensive vulnerability without James Tarkowski. Haaland stays despite a blank and an away match at Arsenal: Palmer is judged the more pressing premium sale, and there is no compelling use for Haaland’s funds. Up front, Barry remains a hold despite worsening fixtures because of his secure minutes and chance volume, although Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the preferred budget forward for the next three gameweeks thanks to home fixtures against Coventry and Ipswich. Longer term, Freeman wants three Liverpool assets, potentially including Isak, and is considering a Gameweek 14 Free Hit to target Leeds v Ipswich, Bournemouth v Hull, Manchester United and Liverpool assets.
key_points: Tom plans to use two Gameweek 12 transfers, most likely Kevin Schade and Anton Stach out for Morgan Gibbs-White and Florian Wirtz.
Gibbs-White is a captaincy contender against Chelsea if Moises Caicedo is unavailable, with penalties and secure minutes strengthening his appeal.
Wirtz is preferred to Szoboszlai for open-play threat and broader routes to points, despite Szoboszlai’s set pieces.
Cole Palmer is expected to be sold soon, likely after Crystal Palace, before Chelsea’s difficult run against Liverpool, Manchester City and Aston Villa.
Nicolas Jackson is the current captain against Ipswich, but Isak would be preferred if available because Liverpool’s attack looks stronger and Everton miss Tarkowski.
Haaland remains a hold despite facing Arsenal; selling Palmer is a greater priority and there is no obvious upgrade requiring Haaland’s budget.
Barry is retained for his nailed role and chance volume, while Calvert-Lewin is the preferred cheap forward for the next three gameweeks.
Gameweek 14 is a potential Free Hit week, with Leeds, Bournemouth, Manchester United and Liverpool all offering attractive fixtures.

items.title: FPL GAMEWEEK 12 PREVIEW! 🔮 TOP 5 GOALKEEPERS 🧤 WIRTZ IN? 🇩🇪 | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: David Raya injury puts Arsenal defence under scrutiny as Florian Wirtz emerges as Liverpool’s best buy
items.summary:
David Raya’s availability dominates Gameweek 12 planning after Arsenal confirm his injury is less serious than first feared. He misses the Champions League tie with Borussia Dortmund and may yet be available against Manchester City, although a return within the next three or four weeks appears more realistic. With Arsenal’s fixtures improving markedly from Gameweek 15/16, selling Raya immediately could prove premature. The preferred approach is to upgrade a non-playing reserve goalkeeper and bench Raya unless later news confirms a lengthy absence; Arsenal’s defence looks notably weaker with Kepa deputising, while Saliba’s return, Calafiori’s minutes and Gabriel’s price complicate alternative routes into the back line.

For a goalkeeper replacement, Trafford is the preferred long-term option because Leeds have strong defensive numbers and favourable home fixtures against Coventry, Ipswich and Fulham in the next five, albeit alongside trips to Manchester City and Liverpool. Kinsley is the cheap £4.4m alternative, with Spurs posting good defensive data, while Verbruggen and Petrovic are strongest for managers needing one goalkeeper to start every week. Verbruggen is more appealing if Raya is sold, rather than retained, because Brighton’s squad slot is valuable. Alisson is a viable direct Raya replacement but is judged too expensive relative to the cheaper choices, while Bournemouth goalkeeper coverage risks blocking access to their more attractive outfield assets.

Liverpool are becoming an increasingly compelling investment after their win over Manchester United, with Everton, Sunderland, Chelsea, Leeds and Spurs next. Their underlying attacking and defensive numbers are improving, and Florian Wirtz is the standout purchase: his recent performances suggest he is beginning to translate international form into Premier League returns, and consistent midfield options are scarce. Alexander Isak remains a strong but expensive forward option, yet cheaper reliable strikers such as Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Jackson and Barry make Wirtz the easier fit for most squad structures. A cheaper Liverpool defensive differential such as Schalke is preferred to Virgil van Dijk, while Szoboszlai at £6.7m offers a potential penalty route but carries uncertainty over spot-kick duties.

For Gameweek 12, Leeds have the best clean-sheet projection at home to Coventry, making Mohammed a leading defensive buy and Calvert-Lewin a leading captaincy candidate. Brighton assets, including Pascal Gross and attacking defenders, also rate well, while Manchester City’s trip to Arsenal suppresses Erling Haaland’s appeal. Manchester United’s good upcoming fixture run is not enough to justify immediate investment after their poor display against Liverpool, though Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo become differential gambles if United improve in Europe. A Free Hit in Gameweek 14, when United host Coventry, may be a safer way to exploit their upside without holding their players long term.

Hits remain acceptable when they solve lasting squad problems rather than chase a one-week return: a minus four for Raya and other unwanted players can be justified if the replacements are strong over several weeks. Wildcard in Gameweek 12 is viable for teams needing a major restructure, otherwise Gameweek 16 offers a fixture swing. Bench Boost should be used at the first genuinely strong opportunity rather than held for Christmas congestion, while there is no standout Triple Captain option in Gameweek 12. A sample wildcard retains Haaland alongside Calvert-Lewin and Jackson, adds Wirtz, Tavernier and Gross, and uses a Trafford-Kinsley goalkeeper rotation if Raya is ruled out.
key_points: Keep David Raya if his absence is limited; upgrade a non-playing backup goalkeeper rather than sell Arsenal’s long-term defensive route immediately.
Trafford is the preferred rotating goalkeeper option, while Verbruggen or Petrovic are better for managers who need one starter every Gameweek.
Arsenal’s defensive appeal falls if Kepa starts against Manchester City, although Gabriel remains the most secure premium outfield route for a Gameweek 12 wildcard.
Captain Dominic Calvert-Lewin at home to Coventry is a leading alternative to Erling Haaland, with Leeds the only side projected above a 40% clean-sheet chance.
Buy Florian Wirtz as the preferred Liverpool attacker; Isak is attractive but harder to afford alongside reliable cheaper forwards.
Avoid rushing into Manchester United players despite their fixture run; a Gameweek 14 Free Hit for Coventry at home can target them without long-term risk.
Use a minus four only for transfers that improve the squad beyond one Gameweek, particularly if Raya’s injury creates wider structural problems.
Consider playing Bench Boost early when the full squad is healthy, and do not use Triple Captain in Gameweek 12.

items.title: 🚨 Raya update 🚨 FPL GW12 Transfer Tips 🔥
items.headline: Raya injury pushes FPL managers towards Kinsky as Calvert-Lewin and Gibbs-White top transfer targets
items.summary:
David Raya’s injury appears short term after Mikel Arteta reports encouraging tests and no need for surgery, with some indications he could return for Manchester City. Selling Raya is therefore discouraged for managers who still view him as a strong longer-term Arsenal asset, particularly with fixtures improving from Gameweek 15-16. Instead, upgrading the reserve goalkeeper to Tottenham’s 4.4m Antonin Kinsky is the preferred cover: he can start against Sunderland in Gameweek 12, Fulham in Gameweek 13 and Hull in Gameweek 15, while avoiding the need to use a transfer on Neto. A Free Hit in Gameweek 12 is viable only if Raya’s Gameweek 13 return is virtually certain; otherwise, saving it, potentially for Gameweek 14, is safer. Fielding 10 players is only acceptable in an extreme one-transfer, no-bank scenario.

Manchester United’s improving fixtures make Bryan Mbeumo tempting, but uncertainty under Mauricio Pochettino — including Mbeumo being substituted before Matheus Cunha in the Liverpool red-card game — makes a new purchase risky. Existing owners should hold for Brentford at home and Coventry in Gameweek 14, but prospective buyers can wait for more evidence from the Champions League and league line-ups. Morgan Gibbs-White is the preferred alternative, despite frustrating recent returns: he is nailed for Nottingham Forest’s short turnarounds, takes penalties and has Chelsea, Hull, Brighton, Sunderland and Everton across the next five. For Liverpool midfielders, Florian Wirtz remains the premium choice, while Dominik Szoboszlai is a strong cheaper alternative due to set pieces and possible penalties; Cody Gakpo and Rio Ngumoha carry too much minutes risk, and Federico Chiesa is less attractive than Wirtz or Gibbs-White at his price.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin is endorsed as a 6.0m forward for Coventry and Ipswich at home in Gameweeks 12 and 14, plus a useful longer-term run from Gameweek 16. He is nailed, on penalties and particularly useful in deep squads that can bench him for Manchester City away in Gameweek 13 and Liverpool away in Gameweek 15. However, managers committed to a Gameweek 14 Free Hit have less need to buy him immediately. Among Leeds defenders, Jaka Bijol is preferred to Jayden Bogle because his DefCon output gives him a steadier floor, although Bogle’s attacking data makes him a perfectly credible cheaper alternative. Noah Okafor is a high-upside 5.7m differential after his 15-point haul, but his uncertain starts and frequent early substitutions make him an avoid for managers prioritising reliable minutes.

Micky van de Ven remains a good 5.2m defender, with exceptional consistency since Gameweek 3 through clean sheets, DefCon, bonus and goal threat, but prospective buyers should recognise that Tottenham’s fixture run now worsens. Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester City, Bournemouth and Brighton all arrive before Gameweek 19, so his recent return rate may fall and he is far from essential. Kevin Schade, meanwhile, is a sell after being benched against Everton, with no guarantee of a return for Manchester United away and difficult Arsenal and Manchester City fixtures to follow. If funds allow, move up to Wirtz or Szoboszlai; cheaper replacements include Enzo Le Fée, Rodoni and possibly Belloumi. Aston Villa’s next fixtures are appealing, but John McGinn is an avoid after two benchings in five Gameweeks. Manzambi is holdable but carries early-substitution risk, while the 4.9m Allison is the most acceptable low-cost Villa punt because he can sit as an eighth attacker if his minutes deteriorate.
key_points: Hold Raya if possible: his injury looks short term, and buying Tottenham’s 4.4m Kinsky as cover is preferable to a Raya sale or a goalkeeper double-up with Neto.
Avoid a Gameweek 12 Free Hit unless Raya is almost certain to return in Gameweek 13; saving the chip for Gameweek 14 has greater appeal for squads light on Bournemouth and Manchester United players.
Hold Mbeumo if owned, but delay buying him until Pochettino’s preferred Manchester United attack and Mbeumo’s minutes become clearer.
Gibbs-White is favoured over a new Mbeumo or Morgan Rogers purchase because of penalties, secure minutes and a stronger near-term fixture run.
Buy Calvert-Lewin if a forward replacement is needed, but ideally have bench cover for Leeds’ Gameweek 13 trip to Manchester City and Gameweek 15 trip to Liverpool.
Prefer Murmurovic over Bogle for Leeds defensive cover because of his reliable DefCon potential, although Bogle offers stronger attacking numbers.
Sell Schade after his Everton benching; Wirtz and Szoboszlai are the preferred upgrades, while Le Fée and Rodoni are viable budget replacements.
Avoid buying McGinn and be cautious with Manzambi and Okafor because of rotation and early-substitution risks.

items.title: FPL GW12 TRANSFER TIPS! | Top Picks Tier List for Gameweek 12 - 2026/27! ⭐
items.headline: Hold Haaland through Arsenal, but Bruno Fernandes emerges as the Gameweek 14-15 captaincy play
items.summary:
Gameweek 11’s disappointing returns do not justify wholesale panic selling. Erling Haaland remains a hold despite Manchester City’s trip to Arsenal in Gameweek 12: he is unlikely to be the preferred captain and can even be benched by aggressive managers, but his underlying numbers remain strong and the recent three-game scoring lull is viewed as temporary. Nicolas Jackson is the standout forward to own or buy, with Ipswich and Crystal Palace among a very favourable upcoming run, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin is both a hold and a viable purchase for his home fixtures against Coventry and Ipswich, especially for managers who can bench or Free Hit around his tougher weeks.

The most urgent forward exits are Wissa, Joao Pedro and Thiago. Wissa carries major rotation risk in an unconvincing Newcastle attack, Joao Pedro has no reliable return date and is unlikely to be trusted for the Gameweek 13 midweek match against Crystal Palace, while Thiago remains suspended with difficult fixtures ahead. Kostoulas, Havertz, Marmoush and Barry are holds only if there is no compelling replacement: Kostoulas and Marmoush face increased rotation risk during the coming midweek schedule, while Barry’s excellent underlying numbers and low price make him benchable rather than an automatic sale.

In midfield, keep Manzambi for Aston Villa’s excellent run of Ipswich, Everton, Crystal Palace and Coventry, accepting that his minutes may be managed after injury. Morgan Rogers is secure for minutes through Crystal Palace in Gameweek 13, while Bruno Fernandes is worth retaining and buying despite Manchester United’s heavy loss to Liverpool; he is the side’s likeliest scorer, has a kind run including Brentford, Newcastle, Coventry and Crystal Palace, and offers captaincy potential in Gameweeks 14 and 15 when City face Brentford and Chelsea. Mbeumo is a softer hold, while Cole Palmer is close to a sell because his chances have been low quality and he has not scored from open play since Gameweek 2; Crystal Palace at home in Gameweek 13 is the main reason to delay the move.

Defensively, do not overreact to Brighton’s Gameweek 11 collapse: Vuskovic remains a hold, while Arsenal’s Gabriel and Calafiori are playable even against City given Arsenal’s credible clean-sheet odds. Lewis Hall, Gvardiol and Ben White are clearer exits because of poor fixtures, injuries or rotation. For new defenders, Van Hecke is the leading all-round buy, particularly for managers planning a Gameweek 14 Free Hit; Mahmovic and Vuskovic offer higher ceilings but require cover in tougher fixtures. Verbruggen is the preferred goalkeeper purchase, with Kinsky a strong £4.4m alternative. David Raya should be held if possible, as his elbow issue is not serious and he targets a Gameweek 12 return against City.
key_points: Buy Nicolas Jackson as the leading forward option for the favourable Ipswich and Crystal Palace fixtures, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin is a strong short-term alternative.
Keep Haaland through Gameweek 12 despite the Arsenal fixture, but look to Bruno Fernandes for captaincy in Gameweeks 14 and 15.
Sell Wissa, Joao Pedro and Thiago due to rotation risk, uncertain injury timing and suspension respectively.
Keep Manzambi for Aston Villa’s next four fixtures, but recognise that his minutes carry some post-injury risk.
Palmer is a likely sell after Gameweek 13 unless his underlying chance quality improves; Crystal Palace at home is his final major appeal.
Hold Brighton defenders rather than reacting to Gameweek 11, and target Van Hecke, Mahmovic or Vuskovic for defensive transfers based on squad rotation needs.
Do not rush Raya out: he is expected to miss Europe but is targeting Manchester City in Gameweek 12; Verbruggen and Kinsky are the preferred replacements if a goalkeeper move is necessary.

items.title: 13 things we've learned ahead of Gameweek 12 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Ryer injury puts goalkeeper transfers on the Gameweek 12 agenda
items.summary:
Ryer’s injury is the most immediate squad-management issue ahead of Gameweek 12. The expected absence looks likely to last at least a few matches, so managers should prepare to use a transfer on a replacement goalkeeper soon rather than relying on a short-term bench cover. Bobby Thomas is back for Coventry and remains a viable £4.0m defensive enabler, although Coventry’s upcoming fixtures limit his appeal beyond bench duty.

At the premium end, Vert is the standout form defender or midfielder to target, with seven attacking returns in the last seven gameweeks and a favourable Liverpool fixture run. Evan Nelson is another in-form option after scoring six goals in six gameweeks. Haaland has not scored since Gameweek 8, making this the logical week to sell for managers already committed to moving funds elsewhere, but his ceiling means holding remains the safer recommendation.

Ponzo starts again while Celiba is on the bench, and Ponzo is expected to start Gameweek 12, though his longer-term security is uncertain. The Kyper completes 90 minutes despite Minteh’s introduction, initially moving to left-back before returning to the wing after Gomez goes off, which offers some encouragement over his place. Williams Barnett also posts a goal and assist at £4.4m, but his starts do not yet look reliable enough for a confident buy.

Several players are clear avoids. Churkey is benched again and should be sold, while Krooppy receives only another 20-minute substitute appearance and is not a viable FPL option. Inmo’s early substitution is less concerning because Manchester United play with 10 men, but Manzambi going off before the 60th minute makes him a risky purchase. McInn does not start and is also best avoided, although existing owners of Manzambi or McInn can hold rather than force an immediate transfer.
key_points: Ryer’s injury is likely to require a goalkeeper transfer within the next few gameweeks.
Vert has seven attacking returns in seven gameweeks and Liverpool’s strong fixtures support a buy.
Evan Nelson has six goals in six gameweeks and is one of the league’s hottest attacking picks.
Haaland has blanked since Gameweek 8; selling is defensible this week, but holding remains the preferred call because of his upside.
Churkey is benched again and should be transferred out, while Krooppy’s limited minutes rule him out as an option.
Manzambi’s pre-60-minute substitution and McInn’s non-start make both poor transfer targets, though current owners can hold.
Bobby Thomas remains a useful £4.0m defender after returning for Coventry, but poor upcoming fixtures reduce his appeal.
Williams Barnett’s goal and assist are promising at £4.4m, but uncertain starts make him a risky buy.

items.title: MY FPL GW12 FIRST TRANSFER PLANS! 🇪🇸⚠️ #premierleague  #fpl  #football  #fantasypremierleague
items.headline: Raya injury forces goalkeeper move as Joao Pedro becomes priority sale for Gameweek 10
items.summary:
David Raya's injury is the immediate problem in a Gameweek 10 squad set up in a 4-4-2, with two free transfers available. If Raya were fit, rolling a transfer to carry three into next week would be viable, but Raya, Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and potentially Calum Chambers create too many doubts to justify patience.

The preferred goalkeeper solution depends on Raya's expected absence. A long lay-off points to selling Raya for either James Trafford or Bart Verbruggen. If the Arsenal goalkeeper is only missing a couple of matches — considered unlikely — the alternative is to replace reserve goalkeeper Bentley with Kinsley, then bench Raya until he returns. The expectation is that Raya has to be sold rather than covered.

Joao Pedro is the other likely outgoing player, as he is still expected to be injured for a further couple of weeks. Alexander Isak is the preferred replacement because he is a player worth owning beyond one fixture, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the cheaper alternative for Coventry at home. Pedro's injury makes his sale more urgent than dealing with Palmer or Chambers.

Cole Palmer remains a possible transfer out, initially with Bruno Fernandes in mind, although Florian Wirtz is now preferred after Manchester United's recent result. Chambers could move to Busquets, but that change is lower priority than replacing Raya and Pedro. No early transfers are planned, with the current expectation to use the two free moves on Raya and Joao Pedro closer to the deadline.
key_points: David Raya is expected to be sold in Gameweek 10 if his injury absence is more than a short-term issue.
James Trafford and Bart Verbruggen are the leading Raya replacements for a long-term goalkeeper transfer.
If Raya is only out briefly, selling backup Bentley for Kinsley and benching Raya is the contingency plan.
Joao Pedro is the priority outfield sale because he is likely to remain injured for another couple of weeks.
Alexander Isak is the preferred Joao Pedro replacement, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin an alternative for Coventry at home.
Cole Palmer could become Florian Wirtz rather than Bruno Fernandes, while Calum Chambers to Busquets is a lower-priority move.
The squad has two free transfers and no early moves are planned before the Gameweek 10 deadline.

items.title: BEST PALMER REPLACEMENTS 👀 | FPL GENERAL'S GAMEWEEK 12 TEAM REVEAL ✅ | FPL Tips 2026/27
items.headline: Trafford emerges as the Raya replacement as Palmer’s FPL value collapses
items.summary:
David Raya’s apparent shoulder problem dominates Gameweek 12 planning, with Arsenal’s goalkeeper pictured in a sling and potentially facing more than a one-match absence. If Raya is ruled out only briefly, keeping him and upgrading a non-playing backup such as Martin Dúbravka to Tottenham’s Antonín Kinský is viable, with Sunderland away and Fulham at home next. But Kinský’s fixtures deteriorate sharply from Gameweek 14, while a long Raya lay-off makes Leeds goalkeeper James Trafford the preferred replacement.

Trafford costs £5.1m but combines a strong immediate schedule with excellent FPL output: Coventry at home in Gameweek 12, Ipswich at home in Gameweek 14, then Fulham, Aston Villa, Hull and Everton after a difficult Liverpool trip. He has four clean sheets, substantial save and bonus-point potential, and a league-leading positive expected-goals-prevented profile among the main alternatives. Aston Villa’s Suzuki is the next credible long-term option, while Brighton’s Bart Verbruggen appeals only if managers have space outside their preferred Brighton outfield trio. Liverpool’s Alisson has attractive fixtures but carries a familiar injury-risk premium.

The midfield debate centres on whether to sell Cole Palmer. His recent underlying numbers are poor for his price, Chelsea’s fixtures include Liverpool and Manchester City, and cheaper midfielders are producing more. Liverpool’s Florian Wirtz, at £7.4m, is the standout replacement after two goals, four assists and exceptional chance creation across his last six matches; Liverpool also top the fixture schedule through Christmas. Bournemouth’s Marcus Tavernier remains one of the best-value assets in the game, although he sits on four yellow cards, while Crystal Palace’s Pino is an affordable differential with Hull, Chelsea, Aston Villa, Manchester United and Sunderland to come. Morgan Gibbs-White is frustrating but remains a hold because Nottingham Forest’s upcoming fixtures are favourable and his chance-creation numbers are still strong.

Captaincy is unusually open in Gameweek 12 because Erling Haaland visits Arsenal while Manchester City are out of form. Dominic Calvert-Lewin, at home to Coventry, is the leading armband candidate, with Nicolas Jackson away to Ipswich and Pascal Groß at home to Newcastle also viable. Haaland is still expected to become a stronger captaincy option soon, particularly at home to Leeds in Gameweek 13, Chelsea in Gameweek 15 and Hull in Gameweek 16, the latter viewed as a potential Triple Captain week. Managers with a Free Hit should target Gameweek 14, when Bournemouth host Hull, Everton host Ipswich and Manchester United host Coventry; Bruno Fernandes is more attractive as a one-week punt than a permanent purchase.
key_points: If Raya misses only a game or two, retain him and consider upgrading a cheap backup goalkeeper to Kinský; if the absence is longer, move directly to Leeds’ Trafford.
Trafford is the preferred Raya replacement due to Coventry and Ipswich at home in the next three Gameweeks, strong save potential and a favourable longer-term run.
Palmer is a credible sell: his recent output and underlying data lag behind far cheaper midfielders, while Chelsea’s schedule worsens.
Wirtz is the premium midfield target at £7.4m, with Liverpool’s excellent fixtures and his recent two goals, four assists and high chance-creation volume.
Tavernier is still an elite Bournemouth pick despite approaching a five-yellow-card suspension, while Pino offers a lower-owned Palace alternative.
Keep Gibbs-White unless a more urgent transfer arises; Forest’s fixture run is strong and his underlying creativity remains encouraging.
Calvert-Lewin is the early Gameweek 12 captain favourite against Coventry, ahead of Jackson, Groß and Haaland away to Arsenal.
Gameweek 14 is a strong Free Hit opportunity, with Bruno Fernandes at home to Coventry and Bournemouth attackers at home to Hull.

items.title: 🚨 RAYA UPDATE 🚨 FPL PLAYERS TO BUY | GW12 ✅
items.headline: Raya injury puts Trafford and Alisson in focus as De Cuyper leads Gameweek 12 captaincy calls
items.summary:
David Raya’s injury creates the key goalkeeper decision ahead of Gameweek 12, although Mikel Arteta’s update is relatively encouraging. Raya does not need surgery, is not ruled out of Arsenal’s match against Manchester City and could miss only a short period, so selling is not essential before further tests and Friday’s press conference. Managers can even buy a playing deputy such as Guglielmo Vicario/Kinsky while retaining Raya if they have a non-playing £4.0m backup. If a replacement is needed, James Trafford is the leading short-term pick for Coventry at home, with Leeds strong defensively and his bonus potential high. Alisson offers excellent longer-term fixtures but carries a significant injury-history risk; chip plans matter too, with Chelsea away in Gameweek 14 making him easier to move out on a Free Hit, while Trafford faces Ipswich at home.

Defence has the standout fixture of the week, with Leeds hosting Coventry and a projected 40% clean-sheet chance. De Cuyper is the top defensive buy and even a viable captain at 5.6 projected points, helped by league-leading attacking numbers for a defender: 4.4 expected goal involvements. He is particularly attractive if he receives his usual European rest. Muharovic is the best five-week defensive transfer at £5.1m, while Gabriel remains the strongest defender over that period despite Arsenal’s immediate Manchester City fixture. Van Dijk and cheaper alternatives such as Jak, O’Shea, Thomas and Mendy also feature well, but Bogle carries suspension risk as he is one yellow card from a ban.

Captaincy is unusually open because Erling Haaland visits Arsenal. Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Bruno Fernandes and De Cuyper are the leading projected options, with Calvert-Lewin benefiting from Coventry at home and Bruno facing Brentford at Old Trafford. A Haaland-to-Bruno move offers major upside because of the ownership swing and Bruno’s upcoming Coventry home fixture, but it sacrifices Haaland for Hull at home in Gameweek 16. The preferred route to Bruno is instead selling Cole Palmer, whose form has disappointed, though holding Palmer for favourable matches against Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace before reassessing is also reasonable.

The midfield case is increasingly about value rather than premiums. Gross and Rogers remain core options, while Wirtz’s five big chances created against Manchester United point to improved attacking potential at £7.4m. Bosai is another improving option, offering set-piece and possible penalty upside, and both are preferred to the more expensive Barcola. Up front, Calvert-Lewin is the priority this week; Jackson is also strong, while Isak, Barry and Evanilson are the best non-Haaland forward options. Evanilson has six goals in six and faces Fulham, whereas Strand Larsen’s immediate projection is good but his next five fixtures make him a poor purchase unless using a Free Hit. Avoid early transfers during the heavy midweek schedule unless an essential price change is involved.
key_points: Hold Raya until further Arsenal news if possible: Arteta says the injury is less serious than first feared, with no surgery required and Manchester City not yet ruled out.
Trafford is the leading Gameweek 12 goalkeeper for Coventry at home, while Alisson is the higher-upside long-term alternative if managers accept his injury risk.
De Cuyper is the standout defender and an unconventional captaincy option, with Leeds’ Coventry home fixture and his 4.4 expected goal involvements strengthening the case.
Captaincy is led by Calvert-Lewin, Bruno Fernandes and De Cuyper rather than Haaland, who faces Arsenal away.
Bruno is a high-upside purchase against Brentford and Coventry, but moving Palmer rather than Haaland is the preferred funding route.
Keep Palmer for Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace if avoiding an aggressive Bruno move, then reassess before Chelsea’s tougher Liverpool and Manchester City fixtures.
Avoid buying Strand Larsen beyond a one-week Free Hit punt; Isak, Barry, Evanilson and Jackson are stronger longer-term forward options.
Wait on transfers through the midweek matches unless a price change directly affects affordability.

items.title: PALMER CAPTAIN?! 🧢 | Chai's FPL GW12 Team Selection & Transfer Plans
items.headline: Palmer armband exposes squad issues as Jackson and Manchester United moves loom
items.summary:
Cole Palmer currently wears the captain’s armband, but that is presented as a warning sign rather than a confident captaincy decision. The squad has several weak spots at once, making three or four free transfers a realistic plan for the upcoming Gameweek rather than a luxury.

Riccardo Calafiori is an obvious candidate to leave. Keeping an expensive defender on the bench is seen as poor use of funds, particularly when a replacement can offer an immediate favourable fixture as well as a stronger medium-term schedule. The priority is to turn bench value into an active starter without making a short-term move that creates another transfer problem later.

Gonzalo is another concern after losing his place, and Nicolas Jackson is the proposed attacking replacement. Jackson offers a strong fixture in the upcoming Gameweek and has captaincy appeal, giving the move both upside and a clear immediate purpose. Selling an out-of-favour forward also reduces the risk of carrying a non-starter through a period when every squad place matters.

Palmer remains under review, with Bruno Fernandes viewed as a potential route into a revitalised Manchester United side. There is optimism that United’s key attackers could improve under the new setup, making Fernandes a possible premium midfield target rather than simply a one-week punt. A Free Hit is also being considered, reflecting the scale of the fixture and selection problems, although using accumulated free transfers may be preferable if it can repair the squad for future Gameweeks as well.
key_points: Cole Palmer has the armband, but he is not viewed as an ideal captaincy choice and highlights the squad’s lack of stronger options.
Three or four free transfers are under consideration for the upcoming Gameweek because multiple positions need addressing.
Riccardo Calafiori is a likely sale because his price is being wasted on the bench.
A Calafiori replacement should combine a good immediate fixture with a favourable longer-term run.
Gonzalo has lost his place and is a transfer-out candidate.
Nicolas Jackson is targeted as a replacement because he has a strong fixture and credible captaincy upside.
Bruno Fernandes is being monitored as a route into a potentially improved Manchester United attack.
A Free Hit remains an option, but using free transfers to build a stronger lasting squad is also under consideration.

items.title: Is Wirtz essential? 🤔 FPL GW12 Early Thoughts 🔥
items.headline: Raya injury pushes Alisson to the front of the Gameweek 12 goalkeeper market
items.summary:
David Raya's injury is the key Gameweek 12 issue, with the length of his absence determining the best replacement. If he is out only two or three matches, upgrading a £4.0m backup to Guglielmo Vicario or Kinsky-type cover and retaining Raya for Arsenal's stronger Christmas run is viable. If he is sidelined for months, Arsenal deputy Kepa is acceptable at £4.9m, but only if managers can benefit from the improved fixtures from Gameweek 16 onwards; his immediate schedule includes Manchester City, Brentford and Spurs. For a longer-term switch, Alisson is the preferred premium option because Liverpool's fixtures remain favourable deep into the season, although his recurring hamstring issues are the obvious risk. Verbruggen, at £4.7m, is the leading sub-£5.0m alternative if a Brighton slot is available, while Trafford and Petrovic offer cheaper routes with playable fixture runs. 

Florian Wirtz is in excellent form, with seven attacking returns in seven gameweeks and healthy underlying numbers, and Liverpool's schedule makes him a strong medium-term buy. But he is not considered essential for Everton away in Gameweek 12: he has neither penalties nor a major set-piece role, and his current return rate is unlikely to continue indefinitely. Managers needing to replace an underperformer or minutes risk such as Cherki, Foden, Manzambi or Schade can move for Wirtz, but selling Cole Palmer, Mbeumo, Rogers or Gibbs-White purely to force him in is discouraged. Palmer remains poor value at £9.8m and is sellable now or in Gameweek 14, yet his penalties, security of starts and Chelsea's strong fixture run from Gameweek 16 still make patience defensible.

Selling Erling Haaland before Manchester City's trip to Arsenal is a viable differential gamble, especially if it funds Bruno Fernandes, but it is not the recommended default. Haaland is still viewed as the best captain on paper in Gameweeks 13, 15 and 16, with favourable fixtures and elite minutes, penalties and goal threat. Alexander Isak is preferred on a Gameweek 12 Free Hit against Everton, but his minutes in the midweek-heavy schedule and penalty status are less secure. The case for selling Haaland is effectively Haaland plus a midfielder versus Isak plus Fernandes; managers unconvinced by Fernandes should keep Haaland rather than redistribute funds for lesser upgrades.

Manchester City assets carrying rotation or defensive concerns are prime candidates to sell before Arsenal away. Gvardiol, Rúben Dias and other City defenders are less appealing than cheaper alternatives from Liverpool, Brighton or Bournemouth, while Cherki and Foden lack sufficient minutes security. Doku and Savinho are possible holds because of price, recent starts and upcoming fixtures, but remain differential risks. Fernandes is worth considering as an expensive, low-owned four-week punt despite Manchester United's league position: he is nailed for 90 minutes, takes penalties and has Brentford at home, Newcastle away, Coventry at home and Crystal Palace away, with captaincy appeal particularly against Coventry in Gameweek 14.

For the current squad, the central decision is whether to buy Fernandes now or preserve transfers and Free Hit in Gameweek 14. A Raya-to-Alisson move supports a Liverpool-heavy plan and a Gameweek 14 Free Hit, allowing managers to target Manchester United versus Coventry and Bournemouth versus Hull without committing to Fernandes long term. Buying Fernandes for Palmer instead makes a Gameweek 14 Free Hit less attractive and points towards Trafford or Petrovic in goal, plus a possible move for Murillo/Murmuvić in defence. The preferred low-transfer route leans towards replacing Raya, strengthening Liverpool coverage and retaining flexibility rather than forcing Fernandes or Murmuvić immediately.
key_points: Wait for Mikel Arteta's update on David Raya before deciding whether to hold him, buy Arsenal deputy Kepa, or move permanently to another goalkeeper.
Alisson is the preferred long-term Raya replacement because Liverpool's fixtures stay strong, while Verbruggen is the standout cheaper option at £4.7m.
Do not force Florian Wirtz in by selling viable Gameweek 12 assets such as Palmer, Mbeumo or Gibbs-White; target him instead as a replacement for genuine weak links or minutes risks.
Haaland is a hold for most managers despite Arsenal away in Gameweek 12, with captaincy preference in Gameweeks 13, 15 and 16.
A Haaland sale only makes real sense if it funds Bruno Fernandes; managers who do not want Fernandes should avoid the move.
Sell Manchester City defenders and unreliable attackers such as Gvardiol, Cherki and Foden if a transfer is available, with Doku and Savinho the more defensible low-cost holds.
Bruno Fernandes is a differential captaincy option for Gameweek 14 against Coventry, but buying him now can require later transfers to release funds.
Free Hit in Gameweek 14 is attractive for squads lacking Bournemouth and Manchester United coverage, and may remove the need to buy Fernandes immediately.

items.title: RAYA INJURED ⚠️ 🇪🇸 MY FPL GW12 TRANSFER PLANS 📝 | Fantasy Premier League 2026/27
items.headline: Raya injury forces goalkeeper rethink as Palmer and João Pedro remain transfer headaches
items.summary:
David Raya's suspected long-term shoulder injury is the immediate Gameweek 12 concern, with confirmation on his expected absence set to determine the transfer plan. If Raya is ruled out for an extended period, Bart Verbruggen is the preferred direct replacement because Brighton's fixture run is stronger and he can be started every week. James Trafford appeals for Leeds' home fixtures, including Coventry at home, but Manchester City and Liverpool away in two of the next four would ideally require a second goalkeeper such as Kinsky. That two-transfer commitment is difficult to justify while Cole Palmer, João Pedro and potentially Riccardo Calafiori also need attention. If Raya is only out briefly, upgrading Ben Bentley to the £4.4m Kinsky and retaining Raya is the alternative.

Raya's absence also weakens the case for Arsenal defensive cover. Calafiori is currently benched against Manchester City and could be sold for Vuskovic, whose Newcastle home fixture is an attractive entry point, with a five-man defence then viable. Gabriel is the preferred Arsenal defensive upgrade but is unaffordable without selling Palmer. Moving on from both Raya and Calafiori would leave no Arsenal defenders, which is uncomfortable, but may be acceptable given the uncertainty over Kepa deputising and the ability to return later.

Palmer is viewed as overpriced and out of form despite Chelsea facing Nottingham Forest away and Crystal Palace at home. A Manchester United midfielder, particularly Bruno Fernandes, was the intended replacement route, but United's latest performance does not justify an immediate purchase. Their Champions League display is worth monitoring for tactical clues around Fernandes, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha, but there is no urgency to chase them. Florian Wirtz offers a cheaper Palmer replacement after a goal and assist, while Liverpool's favourable longer-term schedule beginning at Everton makes him appealing; Martin Odegaard is another option after improved recent returns.

João Pedro remains a sell candidate if he is still unavailable, though goalkeeper cover takes priority. Alexander Isak is attractive if funds can be released, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin has a strong immediate fixture at home to Coventry after a major haul, Evanilson has scored six in six ahead of Fulham away, and Barry offers reliable big-chance potential despite a less ideal entry week. The likely priority order is Raya to Verbruggen if the injury is long term, then João Pedro or Calafiori out; Palmer may have to survive another week and could even be benched at Forest, although Antonio Silva away to Fulham is the more likely bench option. No early moves are planned before injury updates and midweek European matches.
key_points: Wait for a definitive Raya prognosis: a long absence points to Raya-to-Verbruggen, while a short lay-off makes Bentley-to-Kinsky viable.
Trafford is appealing for Leeds' home fixtures but City and Liverpool away make his route difficult without also buying Kinsky.
Calafiori-to-Vuskovic is a viable second transfer, particularly if a five-defender formation is used in Gameweek 12.
Palmer is a priority sale in principle, but Nottingham Forest away and Crystal Palace at home may justify delaying the move while larger problems are addressed.
Bruno Fernandes and other Manchester United attackers are not buys yet unless their Champions League performance shows a clear improvement.
Wirtz is the leading cheaper Palmer replacement, with Odegaard also under consideration for sustained form.
If João Pedro remains absent, Isak is the premium replacement, while Calvert-Lewin, Evanilson and Barry provide cheaper forward routes.
Antonio Silva away at Fulham is the likeliest benching candidate, though Palmer could be benched if defensive transfers are made.

items.title: ANY PLANS TO SELL HAALAND IN FPL GW12 vs ARS (a)? 🇳🇴 😡 #fpl #premierleague #mancity #arsenal
items.headline: Haaland sale hinges on captaincy confidence before Arsenal trip
items.summary:
Erling Haaland’s away match against Arsenal in Gameweek 12 revives the case for selling Manchester City’s premium forward and redistributing his funds, particularly with several expensive alternatives entering stronger fixture runs. A month ago, that route looked far less appealing because Manchester United and Alexander Isak had unreliable form and difficult schedules, but the landscape has shifted enough to make the debate credible.

The key obstacle is captaincy. Selling Haaland only becomes attractive if managers trust other premium options with the armband on a regular basis. João Pedro, Cole Palmer, Bruno Fernandes and Alexander Isak are cited as possible captaincy alternatives, but there is not yet enough confidence in them to make Haaland expendable. Keeping him preserves a dependable captaincy option even when Manchester City face tougher opposition.

The immediate fixture case for a sale is clear: Haaland visits Arsenal, while Bruno Fernandes has Brentford at home and both Isak and Chelsea have favourable upcoming matches against Crystal Palace and Nottingham Forest. Moving Haaland on also frees enough money to strengthen elsewhere, including upgrading defence to Arsenal’s Gabriel. The potential gain is a more balanced squad with several high-upside assets rather than one dominant premium.

However, the recommendation remains cautious. Haaland will still score goals, and managers who sell him need the temperament to absorb potential hauls without immediately trying to reverse the move. The strategy requires commitment because rebuilding to bring him back can be difficult. A Free Hit can offer a temporary route back to Haaland in an especially attractive captaincy week, but there are currently no major plans to sell him outright.
key_points: Haaland’s Gameweek 12 away fixture at Arsenal makes a sale and funds redistribution a viable discussion.
Captaincy is the deciding factor: sell only if João Pedro, Cole Palmer, Bruno Fernandes or Alexander Isak feel reliable enough to captain regularly.
Bruno Fernandes faces Brentford at home, while Isak and Chelsea have favourable fixtures against Crystal Palace and Nottingham Forest.
Selling Haaland could finance upgrades such as Arsenal defender Gabriel while improving the overall squad balance.
A Free Hit can provide short-term access to Haaland for a standout captaincy fixture without permanently owning him.
Managers who sell Haaland need to tolerate the risk of his returns, as buying him back quickly may be difficult.

items.title: FPL GW12: Transfer Plans - Raya OUT! ❌ 2x Transfers Used
items.headline: Raya injury pushes Palmer-to-Bruno Fernandes switch ahead of Gameweek 12
items.summary:
Gameweek 11 is a low-scoring anomaly rather than a cue for wholesale changes. Popular captaincy options all fail: Erling Haaland blanks, Nicolas Jackson offers no better return and the alternative captaincy choices disappoint. Double-ups on Arsenal and Brighton defence also hurt as both sides concede, but their underlying season-long defensive value remains intact. Brighton’s 2-0 defeat at Hull is especially misleading: they dominate the chance data, generate 2.24 xG and only collapse after Costa’s late red card, with Oli McBurnie scoring twice after the 92nd minute. Brighton assets remain holds rather than panic sales.

The major immediate concern is David Raya, who goes off with a shoulder problem against Newcastle. Early assessment suggests anything from a two-to-six-week absence, with even the optimistic scenario likely to cover three gameweeks because of the midweek schedule. Managers with only one active goalkeeper should plan to sell, while those with a playing deputy can wait for firmer news. Kinsky is the preferred cheaper replacement in the proposed plan, although Trafford is also considered.

The key midfield decision is whether to retain Cole Palmer. Palmer’s recent underlying numbers are described as alarming: he records little goal threat or creativity, has not scored a non-penalty goal since Gameweek 2 and his few recent assists are viewed as fortunate rather than evidence of sustained output. Selling Raya for Kinsky and Palmer for Bruno Fernandes is favoured over a Raya-to-Trafford move combined with bringing in Calvert-Lewin, because the latter route forces Palmer to stay and creates an unconvincing Leeds triple-up.

Fernandes is a short-term, fixtures-driven punt rather than a long-term value pick. Manchester United’s defence remains highly targetable after another error-strewn display against Liverpool, but their attack still carries quality and Fernandes continues to shoot, create and take penalties. Brentford in Gameweek 12, followed by Coventry and Crystal Palace after a planned Gameweek 13 Free Hit, gives him captaincy potential; he is the leading armband option for Gameweek 12, with Mafeovich a riskier alternative. Haaland is not the intended captain. The wider strategy is to Free Hit in Gameweek 13, then reassess Chelsea assets and potential moves such as Jackson to Joao Pedro once fixtures and minutes improve.
key_points: Do not sell Brighton assets after the Hull defeat: Brighton dominate the match on xG and lose their clean sheet only through a late ten-man collapse.
David Raya is a likely Gameweek 12 sell for managers without a second playing goalkeeper, with his shoulder issue potentially ruling him out for at least three gameweeks.
Kinsky is the preferred Raya replacement, while Trafford is an alternative that can facilitate a move for Calvert-Lewin.
Cole Palmer is a sell candidate after persistently poor non-penalty xG and xA numbers, despite his penalty-taking role.
Bruno Fernandes is the preferred Palmer replacement as a short-term Manchester United attack punt and a Gameweek 12 captain option against Brentford.
Manchester United defenders remain avoidable, but their attackers are worth considering for upcoming fixtures against Brentford, Coventry and Crystal Palace.
A Gameweek 13 Free Hit remains the planned chip strategy, allowing aggressive short-term transfers before resetting the squad.
Monitor price changes closely: Kinsky is close to a rise and Raya and Palmer may fall, making an early goalkeeper move plausible.
